choices.A: Monitor communications between them and facilitate direct collaboration.
choices.B: Teach the Development Team to talk in terms of business needs and objectives.
choices.C: Act as a go-between for them.
choices.D: Teach the Product Owner about the technologies employed during the Sprints.

questions.explanation: A Scrum Master is a facilitator. While teaching is part of the role, the most effective technique to ensure good communication is to facilitate direct collaboration between the Development Team and the Product Owner. Acting as a go-between creates a bottleneck and is an anti-pattern. By monitoring and facilitating, the Scrum Master empowers them to communicate effectively on their own.

questions.question: Who must do all the work to make sure Product Backlog items conform to the Definition of 'Done?'

choices.A: The Development Team
choices.B: The Scrum Master
choices.C: The Product Owner
choices.D: The Scrum Team
choices.E: QA Specialists

questions.explanation: The Development Team is responsible for creating the Increment. This includes performing all the work necessary—coding, testing, integration, documentation, etc.—to ensure that each Product Backlog item they select meets the Scrum Team's agreed-upon Definition of 'Done'. While the whole Scrum Team agrees on the definition, the Development Team performs the work.

questions.question: Of the following choices, what is the most effective way a Scrum Master can keep a Development Team working at its highest level of productivity?

choices.A: Prevent changes to the backlogs once the Sprint begins.
choices.B: Facilitate Development Team decisions and remove impediments.
choices.C: Ensure the meetings start and end at the proper time.
choices.D: Keep high value features high in the Product Backlog.

questions.explanation: The most effective way a Scrum Master serves the Development Team's productivity is by protecting them from interruptions and removing impediments to their progress. By facilitating their decision-making process and clearing obstacles, the Scrum Master enables the team to maintain focus and a sustainable pace, leading to higher productivity.

questions.question: When does the second Sprint start?

choices.A: After the Product Backlog for the second Sprint has been selected.
choices.B: After the customer completes acceptance testing of the first Sprint.
choices.C: Once the architectural changes for the second Sprint have been approved by the senior architect.
choices.D: Immediately after the first Sprint.

questions.explanation: Sprints are contiguous, back-to-back events in Scrum. A new Sprint starts immediately after the conclusion of the previous Sprint. There are no gaps, delays, or intermediate phases between Sprints. This maintains a consistent cadence and flow of work.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a Product Owner's responsibility?

choices.A: Keeping stakeholders at bay.
choices.B: Directing the Development Team.
choices.C: Managing the project and ensuring that the work meets the commitments to the stakeholders.
choices.D: Optimizing the value of the work the Development Team does.

questions.explanation: The explicit accountability of the Product Owner, as defined in the Scrum Guide, is to maximize the value of the product resulting from the work of the Development Team. They are a 'value optimizer', achieving this primarily through the content and ordering of the Product Backlog.

questions.question: Sprint burndown charts are an efficient tracking tool because they show:

choices.A: An estimate of the total work remaining for the Sprint.
choices.B: How many Product Backlog items remain.
choices.C: How much effort has gone into a Sprint.
choices.D: How many hours have been worked by each Development Team member.

questions.explanation: A Sprint burndown chart is a graphical representation of the work remaining in a Sprint. The vertical axis represents the estimated work remaining (in hours, story points, etc.), and the horizontal axis represents time. It makes the team's progress toward completing the Sprint Backlog transparent.

questions.question: One of the Scrum events is the Daily Scrum. What are two intended outcomes of the Daily Scrum?

choices.A: An updated Scrum board to make Sprint progress transparent for the stakeholders.
choices.B: A shared understanding of the most important work to be undertaken next to achieve the best possible progress toward the Sprint goal.
choices.C: An update of completed tasks and of the remaining work so the Scrum Master can plan the next day.
choices.D: A status report for the upper management indicating what each individual has done, will be doing, and what is impeding him/her.
choices.E: New impediments for the Scrum Master to take care of.

questions.explanation: The Daily Scrum is a planning event for the Development Team. Its purpose is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the plan for the next 24 hours. This results in a shared understanding of the immediate next steps. It is also the primary venue for identifying impediments that are blocking progress, which can then be raised to the Scrum Master for resolution.

questions.question: The Daily Scrum is an event that happens every day. What would be three key concerns if the frequency were to be lowered to every two or three days?

choices.A: Too much work is spent updating the Scrum board before the meeting.
choices.B: The Sprint plan may become inaccurate.
choices.C: Opportunities to inspect and adapt the Sprint Backlog are lost.
choices.D: Impediments are raised and resolved more slowly.
choices.E: The Scrum Master loses the ability to update the Gantt chart properly.
choices.F: The Product Owner cannot accurately report progress to the stakeholders.

questions.explanation: Reducing the frequency of the Daily Scrum undermines its purpose. The Sprint plan (Sprint Backlog) would become inaccurate because it's not being inspected daily. Key opportunities to inspect and adapt would be lost. Most critically, impediments would be identified and resolved much more slowly, putting the Sprint Goal at significant risk.

questions.question: Who has the final say on the order of the Product Backlog?

choices.A: The Stakeholders
choices.B: The Product Owner
choices.C: The CEO
choices.D: The Scrum Master
choices.E: The Development Team

questions.explanation: The Product Owner is the sole person responsible for managing the Product Backlog. This includes its content, availability, and, most importantly, its ordering. While the Product Owner may be influenced by stakeholders and the Development Team, the final decision and accountability for the order rests with them.

questions.question: When can a Development Team cancel a Sprint?

choices.A: When functional expectations are not well understood.
choices.B: When the selected Product Backlog items for the Sprint become unachievable.
choices.C: When the Product Owner is absent too often.
choices.D: It can't. Only Product Owners can cancel Sprints.
choices.E: When a technical dependency cannot be resolved.

questions.explanation: According to the Scrum Guide, the Development Team does not have the authority to cancel a Sprint. Only the Product Owner can make this decision, and it is only done when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete. If the team faces issues, they should work to resolve them or renegotiate scope with the Product Owner, not cancel the Sprint.

questions.question: What two factors are best considered when establishing the Sprint length?

choices.A: The risk of being disconnected from the stakeholders
choices.B: The frequency at which team formation can be changed
choices.C: The level of uncertainty over the technology to be used
choices.D: The organization has mandated similar length sprints

questions.explanation: Sprint length is a balance of risk and learning. A shorter Sprint reduces the risk of being disconnected from stakeholder needs and allows for more frequent feedback. It also provides a shorter cycle for learning and adapting when there is high uncertainty, such as with new technology. The goal is a cadence that is long enough to build a meaningful Increment but short enough to manage risk and get feedback.

questions.question: Which topics should be discussed in the Sprint Review?

choices.A: Sprint results.
choices.B: The Scrum process, and how it was used during the Sprint.
choices.C: Coding and engineering practices.
choices.D: All of the above.

questions.explanation: The focus of the Sprint Review is on the product Increment and progress toward the Product Goal. The main topic of discussion is the 'Sprint results'—what was accomplished in the Sprint (the Increment) and what has changed in the environment. Discussions about the process, team dynamics, or engineering practices are reserved for the Sprint Retrospective.

questions.question: You are the Scrum Master on a newly formed Scrum Team. Which three of the following activities would probably help the team in starting up?

choices.A: Ensure the team understands they need a definition of 'Done'.
choices.B: Ensure the Scrum Team members have compatible personalities.
choices.C: Introduce a bonus system for the top performers in the team.
choices.D: Ask the Product Owner to discuss the product or project, its history, goals, and context, as well as answer questions.
choices.E: Have the Scrum Team members introduce themselves to each other and give a brief background of their skills and work history.
choices.F: Have the development managers for each Development Team member introduce their direct reports and go over their responsibilities on the Scrum Team.

questions.explanation: When starting a new team, a Scrum Master should facilitate alignment and shared understanding. This includes having the Product Owner explain the product vision and goals, allowing team members to get to know each other's skills and backgrounds, and establishing foundational Scrum elements like the need for a Definition of 'Done'. Managerial introductions and individual bonus systems are counter to the principles of a self-organizing team.

questions.question: At the end of a Sprint a Product Backlog item worked on during the Sprint does not meet the definition of 'Done'. What two things should happen with the undone Product Backlog item?

choices.A: If the stakeholders agree, the Product Owner can accept it and release it to the users.
choices.B: Do not include the item in the Increment this Sprint.
choices.C: Review the item, add the'Done' part of the estimate to the velocity and create a Story for the remaining work.
choices.D: Put it on the Product Backlog for the Product Owner to decide what to do with it.

questions.explanation: If a Product Backlog Item does not meet the Definition of 'Done', it cannot be included in the Increment. No credit or velocity is earned for partially done work. The undone item is returned to the Product Backlog, where the Product Owner will re-evaluate its priority and decide if and when it should be worked on in a future Sprint.

questions.question: A Scrum Master is keeping a list of open impediments, but it is growing and he/she has been able to resolve only a small portion of the impediments. Which three techniques would be most helpful in this situation?

choices.A: Prioritizing the list and working on them in order.
choices.B: Consulting with the Development Team.
choices.C: Arranging a triage meeting with all project managers.
choices.D: Alerting management to the impediments and their impact.

questions.explanation: When an impediment list grows, the Scrum Master must act strategically. They should consult with the Development Team to understand the impact of each impediment. Based on this, they should prioritize the list and work on the most critical ones first. For organizational impediments that are beyond the team's influence, the Scrum Master should alert the appropriate level of management to their impact and seek help in resolving them.

questions.question: When does the next Sprint begin?

choices.A: Immediately following the next Sprint Planning.
choices.B: Next Monday.
choices.C: When the Product Owner is ready.
choices.D: Immediately after the conclusion of the previous Sprint.

questions.explanation: Sprints are contiguous and maintain a consistent cadence. A new Sprint begins immediately after the conclusion of the previous Sprint's Retrospective. There are no gaps or delays between Sprints.

questions.question: How is management external to the Scrum Team involved in the Daily Scrum?

choices.A: The Development Team self-manages and is the only management required at the Daily Scrum.
choices.B: Management gives an update at the start of each Daily Scrum.
choices.C: The Product Owner represents their opinions.
choices.D: The Scrum Master speaks on their behalf.

questions.explanation: The Daily Scrum is an internal planning event for the Development Team. Management external to the Scrum Team does not participate. The Development Team self-manages its own work and progress, and this daily synchronization is for them alone. Any management involvement would disrupt their self-organization.

questions.question: Which outcome is expected as Scrum Teams mature?

choices.A: The Sprint Retrospectives will grow to be longer than 4 hours.
choices.B: Sprint Reviews will no longer be needed.
choices.C: They will improve their definition of 'Done' to include more stringent criteria.
choices.D: There is no need for a time-boxed Sprint, since time-boxes are only for new Scrum Teams.
choices.E: A Scrum Master is no longer needed since they are a mature team now.

questions.explanation: A key sign of a mature Scrum Team is its commitment to continuous improvement and increasing quality. As a team matures, they will identify opportunities to raise their standards. This is often reflected by improving their Definition of 'Done' to include more stringent quality criteria, resulting in a higher-quality Increment.

questions.question: Which three of the following are true about Scrum?

choices.A: Scrum is based on empirical process control theory.
choices.B: Scrum is like traditional processes but with self-organization to replace Project Managers.
choices.C: Scrum is a framework for developing and sustaining complex products.
choices.D: Each component of Scrum serves a specific purpose, and is essential to Scrum's success and your usage of Scrum to develop complex products.
choices.E: Scrum is a methodology, where you can pick and choose which parts of Scrum you think will work for your environment.

questions.explanation: Scrum is a lightweight framework for developing complex products, based on the theory of empiricism (transparency, inspection, adaptation). It is not a methodology where you can pick and choose parts; its components are essential and work together. Removing elements of the framework can lead to unpredictable results and obscures the underlying principles.

questions.question: Every Development Team should have:

choices.A: At least one representative from each major software engineering discipline (like QA, Dev, UX).
choices.B: The competencies and skills needed to deliver a Done Increment in a Sprint.
choices.C: One Lead Developer and no more than 8 other members.

questions.explanation: The defining characteristic of a Development Team is that it is cross-functional. This means the team as a whole must have all the necessary competencies and skills to take a Product Backlog item and turn it into a 'Done' Increment without needing to depend on anyone outside the team. Scrum does not prescribe specific roles like 'Lead Developer' within the team.

questions.question: What does it mean for a Development Team to be cross-functional?

choices.A: The Development Team includes not only developers but also business analysts, architects, developers and testers.
choices.B: The Development Team includes cross-skilled individuals who are able to contribute to do what is necessary to deliver an increment of software.
choices.C: Developers on the Development Team work closely with business analysts, architects, developers and testers who are not on the team.
choices.D: The Development Team is a virtual team drawing from separate teams of business analysts, architects, developers and testers.

questions.explanation: Cross-functional means the team possesses all the necessary skills to create a valuable, 'Done' Increment. This emphasizes the team's collective capability. It doesn't mean every member has every skill, but that as a unit, they have the cross-skilled individuals needed to complete the work without depending on outsiders. This structure promotes flexibility, creativity, and productivity.

questions.question: Which Scrum Values are exhibited by not building Product Backlog items that have low business value?

choices.A: Economic Value Added
choices.B: Courage
choices.C: Earned Value
choices.D: Focus
choices.E: Respect

questions.explanation: Saying 'no' to low-value work demonstrates several Scrum values. It shows Focus on the most important work. It shows Respect for the stakeholders' time and money by not wasting it. It also takes Courage to challenge requests and prioritize ruthlessly based on value. 'Economic Value Added' and 'Earned Value' are financial metrics, not Scrum values.

questions.question: What is the accountability of the Product Owner during Sprint 0?

choices.A: Gathering, eliciting, and analyzing the requirements that will be inserted into the Product Backlog.
choices.B: Determine the composition of the Development Teams so they have the capacity to deliver the completed forecast.
choices.C: Make the complete project plan to commit date, budget and scope to the stakeholders.
choices.D: Make sure enough Product Backlog items are refined to fill the first 3 Sprints.
choices.E: There is no such thing as Sprint 0.

questions.explanation: The concept of 'Sprint 0' is not part of the Scrum framework. A Sprint is a time-box during which a 'Done', usable, and potentially releasable product Increment is created. Activities like planning, architecture, and requirements gathering happen in every Sprint. There is no special, separate Sprint for these activities before 'real' work begins. The first Sprint is Sprint 1.

questions.question: Which three purposes does the definition of 'Done' serve?

choices.A: Create a shared understanding of when work is complete.
choices.B: Describe the purpose, objective, and time-box of each Scrum event.
choices.C: Guide the Development Team on how many Product Backlog items to select for the Sprint.
choices.D: Increase transparency.
choices.E: Describe the work that must be done before the Sprint is allowed to end.

questions.explanation: The Definition of 'Done' is a cornerstone of transparency in Scrum. Its primary purpose is to create a shared understanding of what it means for work to be complete. This transparency helps the Development Team forecast how many Product Backlog items they can select for a Sprint, as they know the quality level required for each item.

questions.question: Which of these may a Development Team deliver at the end of a Sprint?

choices.A: Failing unit tests, to identify acceptance tests for the next Sprint.
choices.B: An increment of software with minor known bugs in it.
choices.C: A single document, if that is what the Scrum Master asked for.
choices.D: An increment of working software that is 'done.'

questions.explanation: The single most important outcome of a Sprint is a 'Done', usable, and potentially releasable Increment of working software. An item is only part of the Increment if it meets the agreed-upon Definition of 'Done'. Partially done work or items with known bugs (that violate the DoD) are not included.

questions.question: How much time is required after a Sprint to prepare for the next Sprint?

choices.A: The break between Sprints is time-boxed to 1 week for 30 day Sprints, and usually less for shorter sprints.
choices.B: Enough time for the requirements for the next Sprint to be determined and documented.
choices.C: None. A new Sprint starts immediately following the end of the previous Sprint.
choices.D: Enough time for the Development team to finish the testing from the last Sprint.
choices.E: All of the above are allowed depending on the situation.

questions.explanation: None. Sprints are contiguous events. A new Sprint starts immediately after the conclusion of the previous Sprint. There are no breaks or special preparation phases between Sprints. This maintains a consistent rhythm and avoids delays in delivering value.

questions.question: Who is responsible for engaging the stakeholders?

choices.A: The Product Owner
choices.B: The business analyst
choices.C: The Development Team
choices.D: The project manager
choices.E: The team manager

questions.explanation: The Product Owner is responsible for engaging with stakeholders to understand their needs and gather feedback. This is a crucial part of their role in maximizing the value of the product. They ensure that stakeholder input is reflected in the Product Backlog and invite them to the Sprint Review to inspect the Increment.

questions.question: What is a Development Team responsible for?

choices.A: Resolving internal team conflicts
choices.B: Organizing the work required to meet the Sprint Goal
choices.C: Reporting productivity
choices.D: Selecting the Product Owner

questions.explanation: As a self-organizing unit, the Development Team is responsible for managing its own work and internal processes. This includes organizing the work required to meet the Sprint Goal and resolving any internal conflicts that arise. They are empowered to manage their own path to success.

questions.question: A product increment must be released to production at the end of each Sprint.

choices.A: True
choices.B: False

questions.explanation: This is false. The Increment must be *potentially* releasable at the end of each Sprint, meaning it meets the Definition of 'Done' and is of sufficient quality. However, the decision of *when* to actually release it to customers is a business decision made by the Product Owner. A release can happen at any time during a Sprint, not just at the end.

questions.question: When might a Sprint be abnormally cancelled?

choices.A: When it becomes clear that not everything will be finished by the end of the Sprint.
choices.B: When the sales department has an important new opportunity.
choices.C: When the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.
choices.D: When the Development Team feels that the work is too hard.

questions.explanation: A Sprint can be cancelled only by the Product Owner, and it is a very rare event. The only valid reason for cancellation is if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete. This might happen due to a major shift in business strategy or market conditions that makes the goal of the current Sprint irrelevant. Other issues should be handled through inspection and adaptation within the Sprint.
